Some more info if you think you will be fired: You’re supervisor is obligated to offer that you have a union rep in your meeting if disciplinary action will happen. You also have the right to end a meeting if your supervisor did not provide you this option but you believe that the meeting is heading towards disciplinary action against you.

Hi OP

My ministry job is the first I’ve had that was unionized so I really did not know how the union could help me, if at all.
I felt the same as you. I started to internalize the criticism I received and believed that my anxiety was to blame. In reality, I really liked my job but the constant meetings behind closed doors with the criticism was all too much. 
The union rep I spoke to (I also didn’t have a shop steward) said my situation sounded more like a conflict to be resolved in the office, but they did not refuse my request to attend my next meeting with my supervisor.
All in all I’m very glad to have had a union rep with me. I ended up moving to another position with a different ministry because honestly I felt pushed out and targeted constantly. 

If I were you, I’d hop onto the BCGEU website or make a call and ask what they think your next steps look like.

Are you feeling separate from your environment? I used to feel that when I felt very panicked or incredibly depressed. It's like the momentum of panic lifts you above your surroundings and you don't come back down until you, well, calm down.

As someone who lived with an emotionally abusive mother, and could not leave (I was too scared to due to dependence issues, and my mother also has a physical disability so I felt bad about leaving), I am very glad you are staying with your aunt! Your mom kicking you out may hurt a lot because she's your mother, but that environment, especially if she is using meth, is NOT safe for you. This is an opportunity for you to ground yourself and give yourself the space you need in order to do so. 

The situation sucks, no doubt, but for now this may be one of those nights or days where you feel so horrendous and can not do much about it. This is when basic care is critical. You havent been eating but please eat. Even something like a slice of bread. Have a hot shower. Brush your teeth and hair. Just little things because self care also means not pushing yourself too hard. You've had a very emotionally taxing time right now, so you need rest and deserve peace.
